nodes.summary: An assertion is a predicate on program states: it assigns a proposition to each state. Assertions serve as the preconditions and postconditions of Hoare triples.
nodes.title: Assertion

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a boolean expression, $c$ a command, $n$ a natural number and $s$, $t$ states. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in $t$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$, then the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ runs from $s$ to $t$ in the big-step semantics.
nodes.title: Counted loop runs are big-step executions

nodes.summary: For all assertions $P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, if the total-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is valid, then it is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic.
nodes.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic is relatively complete

nodes.summary: For all assertions $P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, if the total-correctness triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid, then it is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic.
nodes.title: Relative completeness of total-correctness Hoare logic

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a boolean expression, $c$ a command and $s$ a state. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in a state $t$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body and also exits in a state $t'$ after exactly $m$ executions of the body, then $n = m$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the loop iteration count

nodes.summary: For all assertions $P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, if the triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic, then it is derivable in partial-correctness Hoare logic.
nodes.title: Total-correctness derivations give partial-correctness derivations

nodes.summary: For all assertions $P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, the partial-correctness triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is derivable if and only if, for all states $s$ and $t$ such that $P$ holds at $s$ and the pair $(s, t)$ lies in the relational denotation of $c$, $Q$ holds at $t$.
nodes.title: Partial-correctness Hoare logic matches the denotational semantics

nodes.summary: For every Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$, the triple is derivable in the default inference system on Hoare triples, which is partial-correctness Hoare logic, if and only if it is valid for partial correctness.
nodes.title: Derivability in the default inference system on Hoare triples is validity

nodes.summary: A Hoare triple, given by a precondition $P$, a command $c$ and a postcondition $Q$, is derivable in the default inference system on Hoare triples, which is partial-correctness Hoare logic, if and only if it is valid for partial correctness.
nodes.title: Partial-correctness Hoare logic as an inference system

nodes.summary: A Hoare triple, given by a precondition $P$, a command $c$ and a postcondition $Q$, is derivable in the inference system on Hoare triples tagged total correctness, which is total-correctness Hoare logic, if and only if it is valid for total correctness.
nodes.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic as an inference system

nodes.summary: For every command $c$ and every assertion $Q$, the triple whose precondition is the weakest liberal precondition of $c$ with respect to $Q$, whose command is $c$ and whose postcondition is $Q$ is derivable in partial-correctness Hoare logic.
nodes.title: The weakest liberal precondition gives a derivable triple

nodes.summary: Here an assertion is a predicate on states, and an assertion $P$ entails an assertion $P'$ when every state satisfying $P$ satisfies $P'$. For an assertion $P$ and a Boolean expression $b$, the assertion $P \land b$ holds in a state when $P$ holds there and $b$ evaluates to true in it, and the assertion $P \land \lnot b$ holds in a state when $P$ holds there and $b$ evaluates to false in it. Derivability of…
nodes.title: Derivability in Hoare logic for partial correctness

nodes.summary: An assertion $P$ entails an assertion $Q$ when every state that satisfies $P$ also satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Entailment of assertions

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command and $s$, $s'$ states. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ has a terminating big-step execution from $s$ to $s'$, then there is a natural number $n$ such that the loop, started in $s$, exits in $s'$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$.
nodes.title: Every terminating loop run has an iteration count

nodes.summary: Let $I$ and $Q$ be assertions, $b$ a Boolean expression and $c$ a command. Suppose that every state satisfying $I$ in which $b$ evaluates to true satisfies the weakest liberal precondition of $c$ with respect to $I$, and that every state satisfying $I$ in which $b$ evaluates to false satisfies $Q$. Then $I$ entails the weakest liberal precondition of the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ with respect to $Q$.
nodes.title: Loop invariants entail the weakest liberal precondition of the loop

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression and $c$ a command. For a natural number $n$ and states $s$, $s'$, the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ runs from $s$ to $s'$ in $n$ iterations when, started in $s$, it exits in $s'$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$. This is the least relation such that the loop runs from $s$ to $s$ in $0$ iterations whenever $b$ evaluates to false in $s$, and the loop runs from…
nodes.title: Loop runs with a given number of iterations

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command and $s$ a state. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$ has no terminating big-step execution from $s$ to any state, then the iteration count of the loop from $s$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The iteration count of a nonterminating loop is zero

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command, $n$ a natural number and $s$, $s'$ states. If the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in $s'$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$, then the iteration count of the loop from $s$ is $n$.
nodes.title: The iteration count of a terminating loop run

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command and $s$ a state. If there are a natural number $n$ and a state $s'$ such that the loop $\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c$, started in $s$, exits in $s'$ after exactly $n$ executions of the body $c$, then the iteration count of the loop from $s$ is such an $n$; otherwise it is $0$.
nodes.title: Loop iteration count

nodes.summary: For every command $c$, postcondition $Q$ and state $s$, if $s$ satisfies the total-correctness weakest precondition $\mathrm{wp}(c, Q)$, then $s$ satisfies the weakest liberal precondition $\mathrm{wlp}(c, Q)$.
nodes.title: Total-correctness weakest precondition implies the weakest liberal precondition

nodes.summary: For all assertions $P$ and $Q$ and every command $c$, if the triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic, then it is valid for total correctness: every state satisfying $P$ has a terminating big-step execution of $c$ ending in a state that satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Soundness of total-correctness Hoare logic

nodes.summary: Every partial-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ that is derivable in the partial-correctness proof system is valid: for all states $s$ and $s'$, if $s$ satisfies $P$ and $c$ has a terminating big-step execution from $s$ to $s'$, then $s'$ satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Soundness of Hoare logic for partial correctness

nodes.summary: Let $P$, $P'$ and $Q$ be assertions and $c$ a command. If $P$ entails $P'$ (every state satisfying $P$ satisfies $P'$) and the triple $\{P'\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic, then so is $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$.
nodes.title: Precondition strengthening for total correctness

nodes.summary: Let $P$, $P'$ and $Q$ be assertions and $c$ a command. If $P$ entails $P'$ (every state satisfying $P$ satisfies $P'$) and the partial-correctness triple $\{P'\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in the partial-correctness proof system, then so is $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$.
nodes.title: Precondition strengthening for partial correctness

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an assertion, $x$ a variable and $e$ an arithmetic expression. The assertion $P[e/x]$ holds in a state $s$ exactly when $P$ holds in the state obtained from $s$ by setting the value of $x$ to the value of $e$ in $s$.
nodes.title: Substitution in an assertion

nodes.summary: For all assertions $P$, $Q$ (predicates on states) and every IMP command $c$, the triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in the total-correctness Hoare logic if and only if for every state $s$ satisfying $P$ there is a state $s'$ such that $(s, s')$ lies in the relational denotation of $c$ and $s'$ satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic is sound and complete for the denotational semantics

nodes.summary: For all assertions $P$, $Q$ (predicates on states) and every IMP command $c$, the triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in the total-correctness Hoare logic if and only if it is totally valid.
nodes.title: Soundness and relative completeness of total-correctness Hoare logic

nodes.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and every assertion $Q$ (a predicate on states), the triple $\{\mathrm{wp}(c, Q)\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ is derivable in the total-correctness Hoare logic. Here $\mathrm{wp}(c, Q)$ is the semantic weakest precondition: it holds in a state $s$ exactly when there is a terminating execution of $c$ from $s$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$.
nodes.title: The weakest-precondition triple is derivable in total-correctness Hoare logic

nodes.summary: Derivability of total-correctness Hoare triples $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$, for assertions $P$, $Q$ (predicates on states) and IMP commands $c$, is the least relation closed under the following rules. In an assertion, $b$ for a boolean expression means that $b$ evaluates to true and $\neg b$ that it evaluates to false. Skip: $\{Q\}\,\mathtt{skip}\,\{Q\}$. Assignment: for a variable $x$ and an arithmetic expression $a$,…
nodes.title: Total-correctness Hoare logic

nodes.summary: If the total-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid and a state $s$ satisfies $P$, then there is a state $t$ such that $c$, started in $s$, reaches $\mathtt{skip}$ with state $t$ in finitely many small steps, and $t$ satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Total correctness gives a terminating small-step run

nodes.summary: An empty type used only as a label: derivability of Hoare triples in the total-correctness Hoare logic is registered as an inference system under this tag, while partial-correctness derivability is the default inference system on Hoare triples.
nodes.title: Total-correctness tag for Hoare triples

nodes.summary: A Hoare triple $\{P\}\,c\,\{Q\}$ consists of a precondition $P$ and a postcondition $Q$, both assertions (predicates on states), and an IMP command $c$. It is the judgement form of both the partial-correctness and the total-correctness Hoare logic.
nodes.title: Hoare triples

nodes.summary: For assertions $P$ and $Q$ on states and a command $c$, the total-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid when every state $s$ satisfying $P$ has a terminating big-step execution of $c$ from $s$ ending in a state $t$ that satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Validity of total-correctness Hoare triples

nodes.summary: For assertions $P$, $Q$ and a command $c$, if the total-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid, then the partial-correctness Hoare triple with the same precondition, command and postcondition is valid.
nodes.title: Total correctness implies partial correctness

nodes.summary: For assertions $P$ and $Q$ and a command $c$, the partial-correctness Hoare triple $\lbrace P \rbrace\ c\ \lbrace Q \rbrace$ is valid when, for all states $s$ and $t$, if $s$ satisfies $P$ and executing $c$ from $s$ terminates in $t$ under the big-step semantics, then $t$ satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Validity of a Hoare triple

nodes.summary: For a Boolean guard $b$, a loop body $c$, a postcondition $Q$ and a state $s$, the state $s$ satisfies the total-correctness weakest precondition $\mathrm{wp}(\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c, Q)$ if and only if either $b$ evaluates to false in $s$ and $s$ satisfies $Q$, or $b$ evaluates to true in $s$ and $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{wp}(c, \mathrm{wp}(\mathtt{while}\ b\ \mathtt{do}\ c, Q))$.
nodes.title: Weakest-precondition unfolding of a while loop

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a Boolean expression, $c$ a command and $Q$ an assertion. Write $\mathrm{wlp}(d, R)$ for the weakest liberal precondition of a command $d$ with respect to an assertion $R$, and let $W$ be the loop $\mathbf{while}\ b\ \mathbf{do}\ c$. Then $\mathrm{wlp}(W, Q)$ is the assertion that holds in a state $s$ exactly when both of the following hold: if $b$ evaluates to false in $s$, then $Q$ holds in $s$; and if…
nodes.title: Weakest liberal precondition unfolding of a while loop

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be an assertion, $b$ a Boolean expression and $c$ a command. Write $I \wedge b$ for the assertion that $I$ holds and $b$ evaluates to true, and $I \wedge \neg b$ for the assertion that $I$ holds and $b$ evaluates to false. If the partial-correctness Hoare triple $\lbrace I \wedge b \rbrace\ c\ \lbrace I \rbrace$ is valid, then so is the triple…
nodes.title: Invariant rule for while loops

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be an assertion (the invariant), $V$ a function from states to natural numbers (the variant), $b$ a Boolean guard and $c$ a command. Suppose that for every state $s$ satisfying $I$ in which $b$ evaluates to true, there is a terminating big-step execution of $c$ from $s$ ending in a state $s'$ that satisfies $I$ with $V(s') < V(s)$. Then the total-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $I$, command…
nodes.title: Variant rule for while loops

nodes.summary: For a command $c$ and an assertion $Q$, the weakest liberal precondition of $c$ with respect to $Q$ is the assertion that holds in a state $s$ exactly when every state $t$ in which an execution of $c$ from $s$ terminates, under the big-step semantics, satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Weakest liberal precondition

nodes.summary: For a command $c$ and a postcondition $Q$, the weakest precondition $\mathrm{wp}(c, Q)$ is the assertion that holds at a state $s$ exactly when there is a terminating big-step execution of $c$ from $s$ ending in a state that satisfies $Q$.
nodes.title: Weakest precondition for total correctness
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
